¿Cómo se calcula la temperatura de equil: How is the equilibrium temperature calculated?
Se impone que el calor ganado y el cedid: We require that the heat gained and the heat lost add up to zero, Σ m·c·(T_eq − Tᵢ) = 0. Mixing 200 g of water at 20 °C with 100 g at 80 °C, T_eq = (200 · 20 + 100 · 80)/300 = 40 °C.
¿Cómo se calcula el calor de un cambio d: How is the heat of a phase change calculated?
Q = m·L, con L_fusión del hielo ≈ 334 kJ: Q = m·L, with L_fusion of ice ≈ 334 kJ/kg and L_vaporization of water ≈ 2257 kJ/kg. Melting 100 g of ice at 0 °C needs 0.1 · 334 = 33.4 kJ; with no phase change, Q = m·c·ΔT.

Con cambios de fase hay que comprobar pr: With phase changes you must first check whether the available energy is enough to complete them. If it is not, the final temperature is that of the phase change (0 °C with ice and water) and only part of the mass changes phase.
Un calentador de potencia P que funciona: A heater of power P running for a time t with efficiency η supplies $Q = η P t$, which is shared among the bodies.
